models.purpose: Size the charging network from a waiting-time bound.
models.summary: US cars in 2030 are 271,561,340 at 0.766 per capita. Daily charges are B0 = 51,676,526. Supercharging serves mu1 = 2 cars per hour and destination charging mu2 = Sy/170 cars per hour, with alpha = 0.2907. An M/M/1/inf/inf queue gives Wq = lambda / (mu (mu - lambda)) at most tw, and lambda = B0 k1 / (Ncp Tw) with k1 = 0.9. Inverting gives Ncp at least the ceiling of B0 k1 / Tw times (1/mu + 1/tw) plus one, split by type through ui and rho_i. The result is Ncp = 11,705,777 piles and 1,463,222 stations, eight piles each. South Korea gets 998,380.01 piles and 124,797.50 stations.

models.purpose: Date the switch from gasoline to electric with a two-species competition model.
models.summary: Electric vehicles x1 and traditional cars x2 follow dx1/dt = r1 x1 (1 - x1/N1 - alpha x2/N1) and dx2/dt = r2 x2 (1 - x2/N2 - beta x1/N2). Replacement needs alpha greater than 1 and greater than beta. Solved numerically with ode45 in MATLAB. South Korea reaches 10 percent electric in 13.03 years, 30 percent in 16.07 and 50 percent in 18.43. Sensitivity: r1 from 0.6 to 1.4 moves t50 from 18.5 to 8 years but t100 only from 55 to 45.

models.purpose: Classify a country as balanced or unbalanced from two indexes.
models.summary: x1 is the share of land holding half the population, from a standard deviation ellipse; x2 is the Gini coefficient. A country falls in R1 when its Mahalanobis distance to the balanced mean is no larger than to the unbalanced mean. The printed distance is d(x, X) = sqrt( (x - mu)^T Sigma^{-1} (x - mu) ), and the decision function is w(x) = (x - mu)^T Sigma^{-1} (X1bar - X2bar), with R1 when w(x) >= 0. Mean vectors are X1bar = (0.270132, 0.411) and X2bar = (0.337678, 0.349). Twelve countries are classified; the United States, labeled balanced, is assigned unbalanced. The text calls the distance martensite distance.
